sections.h2: Why Leland homes can sell fast
sections.html:
Growth defines Leland. The 2025 estimate is 35,731 people, a 52.9% jump from the 23,365 counted in April 2020, and the town had only 13,527 residents in 2010. It sits in Brunswick County.

Newer neighborhoods and a renovated Founders Park give buyers plenty to look at, so an older or worn house needs realistic pricing. Owners usually compare a cash sale, an agent listing and a private sale.

Leland skews toward owners and older residents. Owners live in 80.6% of homes, 28.4% of residents are 65 or older, and only 16.3% are under 18. The midpoint value of an owned home is $398,900, midpoint gross rent is $1,735, and midpoint household income is $91,977. The town counts 13,219 households, and the average commute is 24.7 minutes.

Owners with a mortgage spend a midpoint of $1,722 a month, and those with no loan $650. A large retiree population means many sellers are weighing a move, a downsize or an estate sale, and buyers often arrive from out of the area. Newer builds and renovated parks set the comparison for your house.

Founders Park at 113 Town Hall Drive reopened after renovation, with an amphitheater and splash pad. The town also tracks the Cape Fear Memorial Bridge replacement project. Buyers who ask about either one can be pointed to the town's website.

The Brunswick County Tax Office appraises, bills and collects tax on Leland parcels. The next countywide revaluation is valued as of January 1, 2027.

All real property is valued on its market value and condition as of that date, and buildings still under construction are valued by percentage complete. Owners should receive notices between February and March 2027 and should compare them with the property record card. The assessor can adjust values in an informal review until the equalization board meets. After that, appeals become formal and are argued before the board. Filing after adjournment is too late for that year, and a changed value reaches forward only.

  • 2026 bills went out in mid-August and stay free of interest until January 5, 2027.
  • Visit the David R. Sandifer Administration Building in Bolivia or call 910-253-2829.
  • The Tax Office can name the rates for your parcel.

Leland's budget for fiscal 2026-2027, which runs from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, totals $50 million, and the town says it reflects a 7.4% reduction in the tax rate.

A buyer weighing two houses will compare total tax bills, and the Tax Office can name the rates for your address. State law sets the due date at September 1 and ties unpaid amounts to the parcel, so a closing office pays any balance from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Tax relief for retirees, disabled veterans and heirs
sections.html:
Because Leland has many older residents, state relief programs come up often. A qualifying disabled veteran has $45,000 of appraised value on the permanent residence excluded, with no age or income limit. An unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify. The county assessor takes the application.

Filing is due in the listing period, with late filings accepted up to June 1, and circuit breaker applicants refile every year. An owner can draw on just one of the three programs, so the assessor can tell you which fits.

The home must have been owned and occupied for five years. The deferred difference is a lien, and the most recent three years of it come due on a sale or transfer.

After a death, the clerk of court in the decedent's home county can accept a small-estate affidavit for personal property up to $20,000. A house usually calls for more steps, so ask the clerk or an attorney how to clear title before listing.

sections.h2: Which sale method fits a Leland house?
sections.html:
Weigh speed, price and effort. A traditional listing can reward a well-kept house, though you handle showings, repair talks and a buyer's loan timeline. A direct cash sale moves faster and buys the house despite its flaws, which may mean a lower price.

  • An agent fits an updated house and a patient owner.
  • A private sale fits an owner who knows the market.
  • A cash sale helps when damage, deferred repairs, tenants or an estate house would slow a listing.

Keep every offer in writing, learn who covers closing costs and have your attorney check the figures.

sections.h2: Steps to close a Leland sale
sections.html:
1. Get your latest Brunswick County tax bill and a payoff letter from your lender.
  2. Collect written offers and compare what each would leave you.
  3. The closing attorney searches title and drafts the settlement statement.
  4. If the house passes through an estate, settle who may sign the deed before you sign a contract.
  5. Sign at closing. Unpaid tax and the loan payoff come out of your proceeds first.

A cash buyer does not need a loan approval, which shortens the schedule. If the 2027 revaluation notice has not arrived yet, tell buyers a new value is coming, since it may move the tax bill they will see next.

faqs.q: When is Brunswick County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027 is the effective date, and the county timeline schedules owner notices for February and March 2027.

faqs.q: What is the process to dispute a Brunswick County value?
faqs.a: Request an informal review from the Tax Office, or present a formal appeal after the county's equalization board convenes. Filing after adjournment generally waits for the next year.

faqs.q: When are Leland property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 each year. For 2026 the county says bills are interest-free through January 5, 2027, and that a weekend deadline slides to the next business day.

faqs.q: What does the average Leland house sell for?
faqs.a: The midpoint value for owned homes is $398,900. A particular house varies with age, size, location and condition.

faqs.q: Can a disabled veteran lower a Leland tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly. For a qualifying disabled veteran, $45,000 of the residence's appraised value is excluded, with no age or income cap. A Veterans Service Officer completes the first part, and the county assessor takes the form.
